articles.headline: Ruben Amorim: 'I can't repeat my mistakes' after Man United
articles.description: Ruben Amorim has vowed not to repeat the mistakes of his Manchester United tenure at AC Milan.
articles.headlineJa: ルベン・アモリム：「マンUでの過ちを繰り返すわけにはいかない」
articles.descriptionJa: ルベン・アモリムは、マンチェスター・ユナイテッド在任中の過ちをACミランで繰り返さないことを誓った。
articles.body:
Ruben Amorim has vowed not to repeat the mistakes of his Manchester United tenure at AC Milan.

Amorim lost his job in Manchester after his trademark 3-4-3 formation failed to click. He was only in charge for 14 months, winning just 24 of his 63 matches.

Now in the dugout at Milan, he intends to learn from the past.

"I can't repeat my mistakes of Manchester United, if we don't have the characteristics to play in a certain style then we will adapt," Amorim was quoted by Gazzetta dello Sport.

His Milan side broke from his usual tactic by using a back four in a 3-0 win against Lecce in Italy's Serie A at the weekend. Christian Pulisic, Adrien Rabiot and Diego Moreira scored the goals.

Amorim added: "We'll go back to building with three, but we'll see. Here in Italy, the coaches are very good, especially at going after other teams one-on-one."

Luka Modric, 41, is still a mainstay in Milan's midfield.

- Man United's Michael Carrick concerned about Benjamin Sesko's latest injury

- Carrick quashes notion Manchester United are out of shape

- Michael Carrick keen to find Man United positives, but there aren't many right now

"With Modric, we need to have the ball for a long time, but he's ready to play every game we need," Amorim said. "If we only play transition games, it's not good for him."

Milan are fifth in Serie A after five games, two points behind leaders Roma.

His old side United, meanwhile -- now led permanently by Michael Carrick who initially replaced Amorim temporarily -- have started their Premier League campaign poorly with just one win in five.

articles.headline: Matheus Cunha urges calm after disproving 'Man United will go to Championship' fear
articles.description: Matheus Cunha has said it's too early to write off Manchester United this season after reminding critics they were able to recover from a poor start a year ago to finish third in the Premier League.
articles.headlineJa: マテウス・クーニャ、「マンUは降格する」との不安を打ち消し冷静さを呼びかける
articles.descriptionJa: マテウス・クーニャは、昨季不調なスタートから立て直してプレミアリーグ3位で終えたことを引き合いに出し、今季のマンチェスター・ユナイテッドを見限るのはまだ早すぎると語った。
articles.body:
Matheus Cunha has said it's too early to write off Manchester United this season after reminding critics they were able to recover from a poor start a year ago to finish third in the Premier League.

United won just two of their first seven games in all competitions under Ruben Amorim last season. The 1-1 draw at Fulham on Sunday means they've started the new campaign with the same record.

And Cunha, who scored the equaliser at Craven Cottage, insists the recovery under Carrick last season -- after Amorim had been dismissed in January -- shows that they can still be successful this term.

"Last season was my first season here, and then maybe it was more crazy than this one," Cunha said.

"There was a lot of noise around us, a season without Champions League. Maybe people were saying 'Oh, United will go to the Championship' or something like this.

"And then at the end of the day, we finished third, you know? I feel like inside of us, we still have a lot of trust, we know what we do, all the belief is inside."

United head into the extended three-week international break 12th in the table and without a win for three games.

- Why this 3-week international break is longest ever (and why that's a good thing)

- Cole Palmer withdraws from England's Nations League squad - sources

Cunha says the players are desperate to have the chance to put things right.

But the Brazilian accepted that with Carrick and his players under the spotlight because of their current form, maybe the lay-off has come at the right time.

United return to action in October with a tough run against Tottenham, Atletico Madrid and Como.

"I'm so anxious to play the next one," Cunha said.

"And then we have a big break now. Of course, when you don't win, you feel this kind of feeling to let's play the next one to win and feel everything good.

"But yeah, maybe it's the moment to be calm, to put the ideas in the right way, to come back. And then of course that could be a big month."

articles.headline: Miami Dolphins end road trip with more lessons than wins
articles.description: Miami's players, coaches say takeaways from 49ers blowout will be building blocks for the rest of the season.
articles.headlineJa: マイアミ・ドルフィンズ、アウェー遠征で勝利以上の教訓を得て終了
articles.descriptionJa: マイアミの選手やコーチ陣は、49ers戦の大敗から得た教訓が今季残りの試合の礎になると語っている。
articles.body:
SANTA CLARA, Calif. -- Just before the final two-minute warning of the Miami Dolphins' 35-13 loss to the San Francisco 49ers on Sunday, quarterback Malik Willis found receiver Ryan Miller for a 77-yard touchdown -- his first touchdown pass of the season and the team's longest passing touchdown since Week 1 of the 2024 season.

Willis wasn't impressed.

"I felt good for Ryan, I didn't feel good for the Miami Dolphins," he said. "That didn't help us. I mean, obviously it helped on the stat sheet, but it didn't help us as a team."

The Dolphins spent the past week in northern California in preparation for what offensive coordinator Bobby Slowik called "a really good challenge" against the 49ers, and will return home from this two-game road trip, after losing to the Las Vegas Raiders in Week 1, with more lessons than victories.

San Francisco scored touchdowns on each of its first five possessions, including both of their two offensive drives in the first half. Dolphins coach Jeff Hafley called the game "a tale of two halves" after Miami watched a 14-6 halftime deficit balloon to a 29-point hole within minutes.

Hafley said his team began the game strongly, but 49ers quarterback Brock Purdy found a wide-open George Kittle for a 40-yard completion on the first play of the second half, ultimately setting up a Kittle touchdown three plays later.

The 49ers went on to score two more touchdowns in their next 10 plays to put the game out of reach.

"We did something extremely uncharacteristic on the first play of the half that went for an explosive," Hafley said. "And we had another huge mistake that went for a touchdown. So quickly, it hit us in the face really hard in the second half. And we didn't coach well enough in the second half, we didn't play well enough. So really disappointing.

"Thought we had a great week of preparation and I felt like we were ready to play better. And the first half we did -- the second half was just not good enough in any phase."

The discrepancy in overall experience between the Dolphins and 49ers was clear in a game between the youngest and second-oldest teams in the NFL respectively. Seven of Miami's top 10 leaders in defensive snaps Sunday have played in the league for fewer than two seasons.

The veteran Purdy had more total touchdowns (3) than incompletions (2), and San Francisco's offense averaged 7.8 yards per play as 49ers receivers consistently found open field. According to NextGen Stats, Purdy's targets created 4.8 yards of separation on average, the most in the NFL this week.

"You've got guys who's [in] the second game ever in the league and they're playing a championship team," linebacker Jordyn Brooks said. "So it's like you don't want those things to happen, but I always look at things from the positive side and I'd rather them happen now, where we can learn from them and build later. As the season progresses, we get better and better.

articles.headlineJa: NBA全チームの2026-27シーズンを左右する可能性のあるスタッツ
articles.descriptionJa: NBAのシーズンを決定づける可能性のあるトレンド、ストーリーライン、注目のスタッツ情報に迫る。
articles.body:
One of my favorite annual preseason traditions is to identify one number for every NBA team, sourced from a variety of data points and statistical categories, that highlights a key aspect of each squad entering the new season.

Last year, for instance, this exercise foreshadowed Jalen Johnson's breakout in Atlanta, the Milwaukee Bucks' struggles in Giannis Antetokounmpo's final season and the Portland Trail Blazers' league-worst turnover rate.

Let's dive into this year's 30 numbers to get a sense for the 2026-27 season to come, featuring all sorts of trends, storylines and statistical nuggets to monitor over the next 10 months.

Jump to a team:

ATL | BOS | BKN | CHA | CHI | CLE

DAL | DEN | DET | GS | HOU | IND

LAC | LAL | MEM | MIA | MIL | MIN

NO | NY | OKC | ORL | PHI | PHX

POR | SAC | SA | TOR | UTAH | WAS

Atlanta Hawks: 108.6

The Hawks allowed just 108.6 points per 100 possessions after the All-Star break, ranking second in the NBA in that span, behind only the Oklahoma City Thunder.

Over the whole season, the Hawks ranked 10th on defense -- and that was before they added Luguentz Dort, one of the most ferocious perimeter defenders in the NBA. Whether Dort and Dyson Daniels can survive on offense if and when they play together remains to be seen, but that duo with Nickeil Alexander-Walker plus Atlanta's other defensive infrastructure could combine to form one of the NBA's stingiest units.

Boston Celtics: 4

In all four of Joe Mazzulla's seasons as Boston's head coach, the Celtics have finished with a top-five offensive and defensive rating, per Cleaning the Glass. Only three other squads in that span have accomplished that feat: the 2023-24 Thunder, the 2024-25 Thunder and the 2025-26 San Antonio Spurs.

That consistent two-way excellence hasn't always translated to the playoffs. In those four seasons, Boston won one title but was upset in the three other series.

Yet after an offseason of turmoil, that consistency should also be encouraging for Celtics fans. Even without Jaylen Brown, their team will likely look like a championship contender on both sides once again -- in the regular season, at least.

Brooklyn Nets: 72%

Egor Demin was by far the best of the Nets' rookies last season, averaging 10.3 points per game and a solid assist-to-turnover ratio while making 38.5% of his 3-pointers. That latter statistic is especially encouraging for a player with shooting questions entering the NBA.

But Demin didn't find many ways to score other than 3-pointers, as 72% of his shot attempts last season were 3s. That was the 16th-highest rate out of 279 players with at least 1,000 minutes last season -- the three players immediately ahead of him were shooting specialists Klay Thompson, Gary Trent Jr. and Landry Shamet.

articles.headline: 2026 MLB playoff rotation tiers: Ranking October pitching options
articles.description: Aces matter in the postseason. Which contenders are stocked with them -- and which are lacking quality arms?
articles.headlineJa: 2026年MLBプレーオフの先発ローテーション階層：10月の投手陣をランク付け
articles.descriptionJa: ポストシーズンではエースの存在が鍵となる。充実した投手陣を擁する優勝候補と、実力派投手が不足しているチームはどこか？
articles.body:
We're just about a week away from the start of the 2026 MLB playoffs, meaning this year's top contenders are lining up their rotations with hopes of making a deep October run.

With that in mind, let's rank the starting pitching options for the teams currently in the postseason field (or deep in the mix) with an eye for how they will be used.

These rankings are weighted based on how often a team is likely to use its pitchers in a seven-game series. The No. 1 and No. 2 starters have much more impact than the others because the playoffs are often about riding your best pitchers and then figuring out the rest as you go. There are a couple of pitchers listed as candidates who, due to the nature of the playoffs, probably won't start but could because of an injury or in a spot-start or bullpen-game situation where an unlikely arm offers a better matchup.

I ranked 15 teams with at least a chance of playing in October, so three of the teams listed below won't end up qualifying for the postseason.

Tier 1

1. Los Angeles Dodgers

The candidates: Tarik Skubal, Yoshinobu Yamamoto, Blake Snell, Tyler Glasnow, Justin Wrobleski, Kris Bubic

Yep, the Dodgers are still tops in this category -- even with the currently injured Shohei Ohtani likely not pitching again this season -- and by a pretty good margin. They could start four arms over a seven-game series that are all better than any one arm on five or six of the teams listed below.

Skubal picked up right where he left off following elbow surgery earlier this year; he posted the third-best FIP among starters this season. Yamamoto is essentially in a dead heat with Skubal, with the latter ranking seventh and the former eighth in pitcher WAR. Snell made only one start before August due to shoulder fatigue and is currently battling a groin issue. He has been fantastic in eight starts in 2026 and was similarly excellent last year over 11 regular-season starts; I'm rounding up due to his pedigree and playoff performances. Glasnow also hasn't been the most durable arm over the past two years, making 30 starts total, but he has been dealing for the past month or so.

2. Milwaukee Brewers

The candidates: Jacob Misiorowski, Logan Henderson, Dustin May, Kyle Harrison, Robert Gasser

Misiorowski, the heavy favorite to win the National League Cy Young Award, has pretty clearly been the best pitcher in baseball this year -- and without a doubt the most dynamic to watch, too. Henderson is a strong second option who has been very good in the second half despite a below-average breaking ball: His fastball shape and changeup are excellent. After making some tweaks in the offseason, Harrison was outstanding in the first half, but his walks and homers spiked in the second half. Gasser is an innings-eater type, while May is a bit more dynamic stuff wise and has been more durable the past two seasons.

3. Philadelphia Phillies

The candidates: Cristopher Sanchez, Jesus Luzardo, Zack Wheeler, Aaron Nola, Andrew Painter

articles.headline: How the Red Sox went from AL-worst to the AL wild card
articles.description: When Chad Tracy took over the Red Sox, they were in last place. Now, they're playoff bound.
articles.headlineJa: レッドソックスはいかにしてア・リーグ最下位からワイルドカードへ上り詰めたのか
articles.descriptionJa: チャド・トレイシーがレッドソックスの指揮を執った時、チームは最下位だった。しかし今、彼らはプレーオフ進出を決めている。
articles.body:
ARLINGTON, TEXAS -- The scene reads like a spy movie set in a minor league stadium: bottom of the fourth inning in Worcester's Polar Park, and the manager is quietly informed that he needs to walk into the tunnel -- but be careful not to raise suspicions. He is handed a phone -- his is back in his office -- and told by the caller to retreat there, close the door and use his own phone to make another call. He is given no clues, only instructions.

It was all very clandestine, maybe unnecessarily so, but Chad Tracy did as he was told. He stood in the tunnel, ended the call with Boston Red Sox farm director Brian Abraham, handed the phone back to mental-skills coach Jake Chaplin, walked up the tunnel to the clubhouse, and then his office, and closed the door.

Out on the field, Worcester catcher Mickey Gasper, now a budding Boston folk hero, looked around and wondered where the hell his manager went.

"Middle of the game, and he's not in the dugout," Gasper says now. "I was confused, like, 'Hey guys, where's our manager? Anybody seen our manager?'"

As instructed, Tracy had called his boss, Craig Breslow, the team's chief baseball officer. Breslow told him the team had fired manager Alex Cora and five other coaches. Tracy was chosen to take over for Cora, starting the next day, April 26, in Baltimore.

Tracy digested the news and collapsed into his chair. At 40, he had reached the pinnacle of his profession, one of 30 jobs in the whole world, and among the many thoughts that swirled through his mind, one carried the clearest signal: Is it OK to be happy?

"You could work 20 years at this and never get this chance," Tracy said this week, sitting in the third-base dugout at Globe Life Stadium in Arlington. "I was playing that mental juggle: sad for my counterparts and friends who just lost their jobs, and ecstatic for the opportunity ahead of me."

He didn't have time to strategize; he just flew to Baltimore to manage his first game and, on the way there, tried to outline a plan. The Red Sox were a mess (or he wouldn't have been there). He knew he had to address the team and the newly reconfigured staff. He knew that communication with some veteran players had been fractured by Cora's managerial style, so there were individual meetings that needed to take place.

He stood in front of the team that Sunday morning, barely 15 hours after plopping into his office chair, and looked out at 26 frustrated ballplayers. They were 10-17, and they were frustrated -- which Tracy took as a good sign, because frustration is far better than acceptance. He figured he had five minutes to find the right words, or at least avoid the wrong ones, because even though he'd managed many of them before in Triple-A, this was something completely different.

"I'm not here to kick the door down," he told them. "I'm not going to bum-rush in here and start changing everything. I'm here to help."

articles.headline: Carrick has an impossible job at Man United after transfer failures
articles.description: Manchester United's players aren't good enough and the club aren't doing enough to rectify that, so where does that leave manager Michael Carrick?
articles.headlineJa: 補強失敗のマンUで、キャリック監督は困難を極める難題に直面
articles.descriptionJa: マンチェスター・ユナイテッドの選手層は不十分であり、クラブもそれを是正するための十分な手立てを講じていない。マイケル・キャリック監督はどのような立場に置かれているのか？
articles.body:
Michael Carrick is failing at Manchester United because his bosses have handed him the impossible job.

A two-year contract as head coach, with the option of a 12-month extension, was Carrick's reward this summer for salvaging United's season from the wreckage of Ruben Amorim's woeful 14-month reign and delivering qualification for the UEFA Champions League. But having given Carrick the job he always wanted, United then told him he would have to do it with one arm tied behind his back after they missed out on each of his top transfer targets and left significant holes in his squad unfilled.

Welcome to reality of the modern Manchester United -- the club that have made mistakes for so long under the ownership of the Glazer family and minority shareholder Jim Ratcliffe that the team are now the equivalent of a house with a leaking roof, broken plumbing and damp on the walls, with nothing but a paint brush to make everything look better.

Carrick, a midfielder who won every major honor at least once during a 12-year playing career at Old Trafford, enjoyed the good days under Sir Alex Ferguson and witnessed the start of the slide under David Moyes, Louis van Gaal and Jose Mourinho. But even though the 45-year-old has experienced the rough with the smooth, it is clear that he has inherited a bigger mess than any of his predecessors.

Sunday's 1-1 draw at Fulham, earned by an 89th minute equalizer scored by Matheus Cunha, ensured that United head into the international break with five points from five games -- their joint-worst start to a Premier League season. And the pressure is building on Carrick.

With less than three years of managerial experience on his CV following a stint in the EFL Championship with Middlesbrough, Carrick is underqualified for a role as demanding and difficult as the United job, but he earned the right to take it on permanently by guiding the team to a third-place finish last season.

However, after being so badly let down by the club's transfer dealings during the summer -- Carrick himself has diplomatically stuck to the club line of seeking value and financial sense in the market -- he has been left with a squad that are not equipped to succeed and will also fail under whoever replaces him if he ends up losing his job soon.

With Casemiro leaving for Inter Miami as a free agent and Manuel Ugarte -- now injured -- deemed not good enough for United, Elliot Anderson and Mateus Fernandes were Carrick's top two targets to rebuild his midfield this summer. But Anderson left Nottingham Forest for Manchester City in a £116 million move and Fernandes opted to leave West Ham for Tottenham rather than United for £85 million.

United also considered Newcastle midfielders Sandro Tonali and Bruno Guimarães, but quickly ruled out a move for the pair, who joined Spurs (£92.5 million) and Arsenal (£75 million) respectively, due to the fees involved.

articles.headline: How to prepare for a potential lockout as a fantasy baseball league manager
articles.description: With a labor stoppage looking very likely for 2027, what steps should fantasy managers take today in order to be prepared?
articles.headlineJa: ファンタジーベースボールのリーグマネージャーがロックアウトの可能性に備える方法
articles.descriptionJa: 2027年に労使交渉の決裂（ロックアウト）が濃厚視される中、ファンタジーマネージャーが今準備すべき対策とは？
articles.body:
For the majority of fantasy baseball managers, an exciting, competitive season has nearly reached its apex. Hopefully, you're still in the hunt for a championship, and will emerge victorious. (Wishing you the best of luck in your quest!)

But for managers in dynasty and keeper leagues, Major League Baseball's 2026-27 offseason might prove to be its most challenging in over a generation.

Unfortunately, MLB's current labor agreement expires on Dec. 1 at 11:59 p.m. ET and, while its owners and Players Association have long been negotiating a new deal, the sides aren't reportedly close on terms. To spare you the gory details, there's a very real possibility of a work stoppage once that deadline has passed.

That's not necessarily a catastrophe! Many of us might have already forgotten, but MLB endured a work stoppage the last time the labor agreement expired following the 2021 season -- one that lasted 99 days and delayed the start of the 2022 campaign by a week. Nevertheless, the league still played a full, 162-game schedule and fantasy leagues drafted and proceeded without a hitch. It's entirely possible that we'll see progress over the coming weeks and 2027 won't even endure a stoppage of that length.

However, it's also possible that the 2027 season will be interrupted, which would have ramifications across all fantasy baseball leagues, but especially those dynasties/keepers. If you're interested in more of the specifics on a prospective lockout and the issues under discussion, ESPN's Jeff Passan recently wrote this excellent primer on the topic.

As it pertains to us fantasy managers, we're focused on properly planning our leagues and dynasty/keeper rosters around any prospective stoppage. What follows are many of the things to keep in mind, and potentially discuss with your fellow league mates, as we head into the offseason.

Make a draft day contingency plan

Our memories of that 2021-22 lockout might be understandably hazy, but the most important fantasy takeaway was that the urgency with which MLB's owners and MLBPA came to an agreement dramatically shrunk the 2022 preseason -- spring training on the field, draft planning for us. MLB postponed the entire opening week's games, rescheduling some of them throughout the regular season and adding the rest as a three-day extension at year's end.

The two sides reached agreement on Thursday, March 10. The 2022 season began exactly four weeks later, on Thursday, April 7. Fantasy commissioners who hadn't been discussing draft contingencies with their league, especially those who prefer live drafts, might have had more difficulty getting everyone on the same page on limited notice.

Beginning those conversations now -- i.e. if we need to draft closer to April, or an agreement isn't reached until April or later, how does everyone's schedule look? -- will prove to be advantageous. That's especially true in a year where Easter falls on the first Sunday of the currently scheduled regular season, March 28.
